page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the e2 server family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, the server demonstrates weak performance, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores are poor, registering in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read and write speeds, with uncached read speeds at 24.13 GB/sec. However, text generation for small 135M parameter language models achieves an average tier rating at 104.71 tokens/sec, though prompt processing remains weak.

The primary tradeoff of the e2-standard-4 is its lower computational throughput and lack of local NVMe storage, which limits its utility for high-performance computing or heavy database operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a balanced resource density for workloads that do not require high CPU clock speeds or advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, development environments, light background processing, and small-scale application hosting.
